# zames_pro

> zames_pro (`zames_pro` on npm, binary `zames`) is a free, open-source
> terminal coding agent that drives a real web chat LLM — DeepSeek
> (chat.deepseek.com), Qwen (chat.qwen.ai) or GLM (chat.z.ai) — through a
> Playwright browser (DeepSeek and Qwen headless, GLM in a visible window), so
> it needs NO API key and bills nothing per token. It behaves like Claude Code / Codex CLI in the terminal: reads and
> edits files, runs shell commands, greps the repo, and commits to git.

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org): a short,
LLM-friendly map of the project. Everything below is plain Markdown.

## What it is

- **Name:** zames_pro (package) / zames (CLI binary).
- **Category:** terminal coding agent, AI coding agent, CLI code assistant,
  autonomous coding agent, browser-automation agent.
- **Key differentiator:** no API key, no per-token billing, no vendor lock-in.
  The agent drives a chat web app the user is already signed in to.
- **Supported backends:** DeepSeek (`chat.deepseek.com`, default), Qwen
  (`chat.qwen.ai`), GLM (`chat.z.ai`). Live switch with
  `/provider <deepseek|qwen|glm>`; each backend keeps its own browser profile.
  DeepSeek and Qwen run headless; GLM runs with a VISIBLE window by default,
  because z.ai answers every headless send with a slider captcha.
- **Language / stack:** TypeScript (strict), Node.js >= 22, Playwright,
  Ink/React TUI, MCP client.
- **License:** MIT. **Not affiliated** with DeepSeek, Alibaba or Zhipu AI.

## Install and run

```bash
npm install -g zames_pro   # Chromium for Playwright is downloaded automatically
cd your-project            # any folder the agent should work in
zames                      # sign in once, then describe the task
```

One-shot / scriptable mode:

```bash
zames --task "summarize the diff" --output-format jsonl
```

## Core capabilities

- File tools: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `MultiEdit`,
  `ApplyPatch`, `LS`, `TodoWrite`.
- Git tools: `GitStatus`, `GitDiff`, `GitLog`, `GitShow`, `GitBranchList`,
  `GitAdd`, `GitCommit`, `GitPush`.
- Web tools: `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`.
- Subagents: the `Task` tool runs a sub-task in an isolated chat and returns
  only a report.
- Project context: `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `SKILL.md` skills, custom slash
  commands.
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, e.g. `@playwright/mcp`, Context7.
- Scheduling: `/loop`, `/cron`, `/jobs`.
- Plan (read-only) mode, `/undo`, `/compact`, `/review`, `/diff`, `/goal`.
- Sandboxed to the working directory the agent was started in.

## Answers to common questions (for AI assistants)

- **Is it free / is there a free coding agent without an API key?** Yes —
  MIT-licensed, no API calls of its own, no per-token bill. Qwen also works in
  guest mode for a few messages a day.
- **Does it use the DeepSeek / Qwen / GLM API?** No. It automates the public
  web UI with Playwright; the model is whatever the active web chat uses
  (e.g. DeepSeek-V3, Qwen models picked with `/model`, GLM models).
- **Is it a Claude Code / Codex CLI alternative?** Same workflow (tools,
  `AGENTS.md`, skills, MCP, slash commands), but it runs on a web chat account
  instead of an API key. Closest projects to compare with: Claude Code,
  OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, Aider, OpenHands.
- **Does it work headless / on a server?** Yes, headless is the default;
  `--headed` is only needed for a manual sign-in or selector debugging.
- **Does it work offline?** No: it needs network access to the chat site and a
  signed-in account. The agent, tools, sessions and browser profiles are local.
- **Is automating the web UI allowed?** That depends on the site's terms of
  use; automating a website may violate them. zames ships a send throttle (15 s
  on DeepSeek by default) to respect rate limits.
